existing_implementation: Native LeRobot ACT classes with minimal history/point observation extensions; old custom FlowACT archived.

policy_pilot.split_unit: episode, before constructing windows; no random window split
policy_pilot.task: complete garment folding; unchanged native success geometry, cameras and control
policy_pilot.validation_and_selection: same full four validation episodes, prior-zero action L1; new development poses never select best
policy_pilot.speedups: smaller task distribution, fewer updates, lossless decoded-RGB caching; retain native 640x480 and end-to-end training
policy_pilot.wall_time: requires new throughput measurement after ACT rebase; no current wall-time promise
policy_pilot.scope: Single garment, single seed, bounded 500-update screening; formal training remains on hold.
policy_pilot.baseline_gate: Expert replay quality and tiny-episode fit establish a valid pipeline. Low ACT closed-loop success alone does not invalidate the task or forbid history/flow comparisons.
policy_pilot.evaluation_scope: User selected one paired development pose for faster visual/control validation, not success-rate estimation.

rationale: Within-window vertex identity links the same point through time.
Shared weights and no semantic vertex-ID embedding preserve point order symmetry.
Metric current position provides robot-frame location while displacement exposes motion.
unvalidated_choices: two temporal plus two point layers
point identities are reselected per observation window

simple_candidate.path: shared per-point 16x8 flatten -> MLP 128->128->128->512 -> ACT tokens
simple_candidate.scope: fixed 16-frame history with explicit masks; no universal variable-length claim

point_encoder.selection: Use the simple 99,072-parameter MLP for this pilot; both candidates fit tiny data but fail the old held-out static reference.
legacy_factorized_path: two temporal Transformer layers per point

gates.name: ACT output/loss/gradient parity with extensions disabled
Existing point-encoder CPU invariants and gradients
Synthetic static/rigid/affine and tiny real-data learning, 200-500 updates per point candidate
Completion validation on held-out episodes and >5mm moving points vs 3NN
Original ACT baseline feasibility, then five matched short policy runs
Additional seeds before any robust policy claim

diagnostic_reference.scope: development train/validation diagnostic; not independent formal results
diagnostic_reference.moving_definition: hidden track maximum displacement over valid past >5mm
limitations: Interpolation receives current query XYZ, exactly as the auxiliary task permits.
Current-space neighbors can join distinct cloth layers at a fold.
GT tracks include occluded past; this is privileged simulation information.
No neural fit, policy rollout or convergence claim is made.

point_encoder_CPU_checks.scope: existing 2+2-layer point encoder, synthetic CPU forward/gradient checks; not learning validation

interpretation: Old six-step completion scores used only two validation windows and cannot be compared numerically with this full 119-window reference.
Passing invariants is not evidence that an encoder learns useful dynamics.
Failure of auxiliary completion does not refute the usefulness of tracked inputs; disable auxiliary weight separately.
Sparse tracks plus current query XYZ do not uniquely determine all cloth histories, especially at folded layers.
GT histories include occlusion and privileged geometry; estimated-RGB tracking remains a separate experiment.
No all-node request, optimizer update or new policy training is performed in this audit.
A simple single-garment task may reach an ACT ceiling; no gain there does not refute flow on harder dynamic tasks.

expert_replay_quality_snapshot.note: Expert replay endpoints, not learned-policy results or a policy success ceiling. Retain all complete episodes; no silent success filtering.

synchronization.gpu17: SSH reachable; code-only task checkout synchronized via authenticated-locally-pushed GitHub commit bundle; no GPU jobs, no remote credentials; session helper absent

evaluation_amendment: User explicitly selected one paired pose before any closed-loop outcome; five500-update training budgets and all scientific model/data/optimizer settings unchanged.
